detail.body:
# Description

Add an opt-in cuDNN OSS (FROST) backward provider to TE's fused-attention path so context-parallel attention can execute the open-source D128 and D256 kernels through the common C++ dispatcher.

The first call prepares a cuDNN Python graph and registers its compiled TVM-FFI backward chain. Subsequent calls bind current pointers, stream and caller-owned workspace directly in C++. Forward and context-parallel communication retain their existing implementations.

## Type of change

- [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)

## Implementation and supported scope

- Reuse TE's optional CuTeDSL/TVM-FFI registration infrastructure. Cache immutable plans per declaration and device, including mask alignment; validate binding alignment, workspace capacity and overlap before dispatch.
- Support SM100 BF16, separate Q/K/V, D128/D256, nondeterministic backward, no dropout/bias/sinks, and unmasked or top-left causal attention. D256 also supports rectangular bottom-right causal attention when Q length is no greater than KV length; Q-longer-than-KV uniform THD falls back in mode 1 and declines in mode 2. Existing forward rejects that orientation for dense BSHD. D128 bottom-right remains unsupported. Dense BSHD lengths are multiples of 128.
- D128 uses native packed THD, including unequal sequence lengths. D256 THD requires an explicit uniform-layout promise, checked on the GPU on every execution, and converts packed FP32 Stats on the caller's stream.
- A separate default-off flag admits causal THD AllGather for CP2/4/8. It preserves physical batch pitches, selects the current Q half by pointer origin, and retains existing gradient initialization for unused rows. No new Q/K/V repack kernel is added.
- Add a default-off D128 output-initialization policy for strict FROST, BF16 GQA and square compact equal-length THD. The PyTorch binding and common dispatcher share the eligibility predicate; an every-execution GPU check validates lengths/origins before the complete backward chain overwrites dQ/dK/dV. Native/fallback, unequal and rectangular cases retain their fills.
- Retain the complete backward helper chain, scratch initialization and grouped-gradient reductions. Add off, fallback and strict-routing modes, plus tests for changed inputs/addresses, nondefault streams, mask-cache separation and CUDA Graph replay. Replay removes the Python preparation callback after warmup to verify native dispatch.

This PR adds the execution path; it does not change FROST kernel algorithms. [TE #3683](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TransformerEngine/pull/3683) separately optimizes layouts and CP copies.

## Dependencies and use

This draft uses the prepared-plan contract in [cuDNN Frontend #1688](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1688), now merged. The original measurements below retain their frozen FE `333278627eb2ccffc5f47da26d733f87a2d0a8aa` attribution. D256 THD AllGather additionally requires the physical-stride support in [cuDNN Frontend #1690](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1690). D128 validation uses the frozen #1688 source with the same D256 fixes; D256 AllGather measurements below use the published #1690 source. Installing #1690 alone does not supply Roman's D128 engine.

A compatibility rerun of the same 62 directed tests passes with zero skips on production B200 using the merged Roman source `c98264fc9222d85dcac747fa9295ed9d8d4b2c47` plus the complete published #1690 patch, unchanged TE native binaries, and the CUDA 13 CuTeDSL flavor. It includes all five isolated metadata guards. This validates the newer dependency, without reattributing earlier performance measurements. A separate default-CUDA-12 probe is rejected by the existing TE compiler gate before kernel compilation; CUDA 12 support is not claimed or enabled. [Merged-dependency qualification](https://sc.talos.nvidia.com/view/home/scratch.yanxu_libs/cudnn_frontend/.te-cp-20261012/results/te_frost_merged_qa_v181_qualified.json).

The adapter is confined to one module and rejects unfamiliar prepared-plan metadata. **The metadata is currently private; a stable FE export contract remains a prerequisite for graduating this integration.**

Install compatible FE source in TE's Python environment with `nvidia-cutlass-dsl[cu13]>=4.8.0` and `apache-tvm-ffi`. Build TE with `NVTE_WITH_CUTEDSL=1` (`-DNVTE_WITH_CUTEDSL=ON` for direct CMake). A newer system toolkit alone does not replace the required CUDA 13 CuTeDSL compiler flavor.

```bash
export NVTE_ENABLE_CUTEDSL_BACKEND=1
export CUDNN_FRONTEND_ENABLE_FROST_ENGINES=1
export NVTE_FUSED_ATTN_FROST=2  # strict OSS backward; 1 permits backend fallback
# Optional: omit fully overwritten output fills for compact D128 GQA THD:
export NVTE_FUSED_ATTN_FROST_D128_NOZERO=1
# For equal-length D256 THD:
export NVTE_FUSED_ATTN_FROST_UNIFORM=1
# Additionally enable the qualified causal THD AllGather layout:
export NVTE_FUSED_ATTN_FROST_ALLGATHER=1
python -m pytest -v tests/pytorch/attention/test_frost_attn.py
```

Warm up each declaration before CUDA Graph capture. Leave the uniform-layout promise disabled for unequal THD and gapped layouts outside the explicit AllGather contract. `NVTE_FUSED_ATTN_FROST=0` retains the existing route.

## Review follow-up at `a7e91a56`

Add `qa/L1_pytorch_frost_unittest/test.sh` for a provisioned SM100 target, with an opt-in hook from PyTorch L0 via `NVTE_FROST_TEST_REQUIRED=1`. It requires the compatible FE/CUDA 13 CuTeDSL stack and a bridge-enabled TE build, checks actual capability, and rejects skipped tests or missing isolated metadata-guard children. The CI owner still needs to provision and enable the qualified lane; ordinary L0 lanes do not inherit the experimental dependencies.

The **actual checked-in QA launcher passes 62/62 tests with zero skips on B200**, including all five isolated guard children. The added D256 bottom-right `Q=256, KV=128` test verifies strict decline, mode-1 fallback against CPU FP64 gradients, and exactly zero dQ on leading keyless rows. It also returns to fallback after strict decline to exercise the cached unsupported declaration. Native source and binaries are unchanged from `cf04d4e1`; no new CP performance claim is attached to this QA/documentation commit.

```bash
TE_PATH="$PWD" XML_LOG_DIR=/tmp/te-frost-qa \
  bash qa/L1_pytorch_frost_unittest/test.sh
```

Changed-file pre-commit, both shell syntax checks, license checks and the exact staged-source comparison pass. [QA qualification](https://sc.talos.nvidia.com/view/home/scratch.yanxu_libs/cudnn_frontend/.te-cp-20261012/results/te_frost_qa_v167_qualified.json). The [comment-only review](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TransformerEngine/pull/3699#pullrequestreview-5555481128) found no new correctness blocker in the supported scope at `cf04d4e1`; this does not replace maintainer approval or the remaining FE export and broader qualification work.

## Validation

Native revision `cf04d4e1` rebuilds the changed common and PyTorch native units with CUDA 13.2, cuDNN 9.27 and PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130. Changed-file formatting, C++ lint, license checks and exact-runtime import checks pass. The existing unused `custom_types_converters` compiler warning is unchanged. All eleven reported GitHub checks passed at `cf04d4e1`, including both minimum-version jobs. All eleven reported checks also pass at the QA/documentation follow-up `a7e91a56`. Full GPU L0/JAX qualification remains separate.

**61/61 directed repository tests, zero skips**, pass through the rebuilt TE C++ entry on a production B200. They retain the 46 existing FP64-gradient, D128 unequal-THD, D256 uniform/bottom-right/pitched-layout, rebinding, stream, fallback and graph-replay cases. Ten added initialization tests check changed inputs, exact OFF/ON agreement, NaN-poisoned graph replay without Python preparation, actual output-fill counts, and native/fallback/unequal/rectangular controls. Five further tests reject changed device lengths/origins in isolated processes, including mutation after graph capture. [Exact-source qualification](https://sc.talos.nvidia.com/view/home/scratch.yanxu_libs/cudnn_frontend/.te-cp-20261012/results/te_frost_nozero_pr_tests_v165_qualified.json).

The following distributed correctness results belong to the preceding `4152a201` build. The newly rebuilt head's full CP16K/A2A comparison is reported separately below:

- **Actual CP2:** B2/S512/Hq8/Hkv2/D256 BF16 causal, all six BSHD/THD × A2A/P2P/AllGather pairs. Native controls and strict FROST pass **96 complete O/dQ/dK/dV comparisons** against CPU FP64, maximum relative RMS 0.003870.
- **Actual CP4 and CP8 THD AllGather:** B2/S1024 and B2/S2048 respectively, Hq8/Hkv2/D256. Native and strict FROST pass **96 additional complete CPU-FP64 comparisons** across 12 ranks, maximum relative RMS 0.005176.
- The companion FE #1690 draft passes its **99-test matrix**, including physical-stride correctness and padding canaries, on a develop base.

Full GPU L0 suites, JAX execution, broader layout coverage and clean sanitizer qualification remain pending. The earlier integration's sanitizer run retained a `Selective device code recompilation in progress` API warning in an existing native-forward launch; this is **not a clean sanitizer pass**, and the later bottom-right/batch-pitch changes are not sanitizer-qualified.

## Complete CP performance at the preceding `4152a201` integration

TE `4152a201` + FE #1690 `5ba587f1`, **D256 BF16 causal equal-length THD, Hq32/Hkv8, CP4/AllGather, 524288 total tokens**. Each node uses four production B200 GPUs: 148 SMs, default 1000 W limit, NV18 links; cuDNN 9.27.0.42, CUDA 13.2-built TE, CuTeDSL 4.8 CUDA 13 flavor, FA4 `4.0.0b35.dev1+gbb25ba3`.

Every shape/node run uses all six provider orders with fresh four-rank process sets: **72 workers, 288 complete output/gradient comparisons and 18 qualified telemetry windows**. Five warmups and 50 timed iterations use the default allocator and dynamic clocks, without CUDA Graphs or profiling. Latency includes **attention forward + backward + communication** and reports the slowest rank. Percentages are medians of paired round ratios.

| Shape / node | Native cuDNN | FROST backward | FA4 | FROST/native change | FROST/FA4 change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 64×8K / B200-250 | 119.82 ms | 102.67 ms | 106.15 ms | -14.31% | -3.35% |
| 64×8K / B200-048 | 119.19 ms | 101.58 ms | 105.42 ms | -14.46% | -3.59% |
| 32×16K / B200-018 | 188.00 ms | 157.06 ms | 170.50 ms | -16.54% | -7.92% |
| 16×32K / B200-069 | 333.57 ms | 272.50 ms | 313.43 ms | -18.24% | -13.06% |
| 16×32K / B200-079 | 335.76 ms | 269.79 ms | 307.66 ms | -19.63% | -12.36% |
| 8×64K / B200-018 | 606.35 ms | 482.19 ms | 558.33 ms | -20.45% | -13.66% |
| 8×64K / B200-073 | 606.86 ms | 487.23 ms | 563.12 ms | -19.72% | -13.46% |

FROST is faster in **6/6 rounds for both comparisons in every row**. These are four tested coordinates: 8K, 32K and 64K have independent-node confirmation with disjoint GPU UUIDs; 16K has one-node evidence. The two 64K nodes pass 576 complete output/gradient comparisons and 36 telemetry windows across 144 workers. They do not establish an original benchmark-grid win rate or extrapolate to D128 or other communication methods.

Peak allocated memory is **61.05 GiB native, 53.05 GiB FROST, 31.03 GiB FA4**. Only the independent native reference is batch-chunked to avoid a separately diagnosed helper-offset limitation; actual CP calls retain the complete shape. Separate vector-load and first-dK/dV reuse changes are excluded. The D128 initialization policy does not apply to these D256 shapes.

[8K two-node qualification](https://sc.talos.nvidia.com/view/home/scratch.yanxu_libs/cudnn_frontend/.te-cp-20261012/results/te_frost_allgather_crossnode_v1_qualified.json) · [Initial 16K/32K qualification](https://sc.talos.nvidia.com/view/home/scratch.yanxu_libs/cudnn_frontend/.te-cp-20261012/results/te_frost_sparse_public_v160_qualified.json) · [32K two-node qualification](https://sc.talos.nvidia.com/view/home/scratch.yanxu_libs/cudnn_frontend/.te-cp-20261012/results/te_frost_public_32k_crossnode_v163_qualified.json) · [64K two-node qualification](https://sc.talos.nvidia.com/view/home/scratch.yanxu_libs/cudnn_frontend/.te-cp-20261012/results/te_frost_public_64k_crossnode_v168_qualified.json)

Separate full-shape trace validation at `4152a201` passes 48 complete comparisons each for D256 AllGather and D128 A2A. All providers execute matching collective signatures/message sizes. D128 backward main-kernel sums are 20.06 ms native, 18.15 ms FROST and 18.06 ms FA4; helpers, forward and copies remain in the full path. These instrumented, separate-process durations are diagnostic, not paired CP latency or a D128 win. [D256 attribution](https://sc.talos.nvidia.com/view/home/scratch.yanxu_libs/cudnn_frontend/.te-cp-20261012/results/te_frost_allgather_attribution_v1_qualified.json) · [D128 attribution](https://sc.talos.nvidia.com/view/home/scratch.yanxu_libs/cudnn_frontend/.te-cp-20261012/results/te_frost_d128_a2a_attribution_v1_qualified.json).

## D128 initialization policy: two-node evidence before packaging

Before this commit, the same native policy was measured as a private patch over `4152a201`, with unchanged Roman `33327862` FROST kernels. The published implementation preserves those native statements; the new build is separately covered by the 61 tests above. These timings belong to the frozen pre-packaging binaries.

Workload: **B64/S8192/Hq32/Hkv8/D128, BF16 causal compact THD, 524288 tokens, CP4/A2A**. Two independent four-B200 nodes use the same six-order/fresh-process protocol, software, hardware and complete-CP timing definition above. All **576 full O/dQ/dK/dV comparisons and 36 telemetry windows** pass across 144 workers with disjoint GPU UUIDs. Untimed audits confirm three versus zero output-fill calls in every FROST arm/rank.

| Node | FROST: initialize | FROST: omit fills | FA4 | Paired omit/initialize | Paired omit/FA4 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| B200-049 | 45.919 ms | 45.608 ms | 44.430 ms | -0.75% | +2.54% |
| B200-249 | 45.453 ms | 45.064 ms | 43.981 ms | -0.98% | +2.45% |

Omitting eligible fills is faster in **6/6 rounds on both nodes**, but remains slower than FA4 in every round. Allocated output sizes and internal FROST scratch initialization are unchanged. This is an incremental benefit for one layout, not an additional original-grid win; percentages from other experiments are not additive. [Two-node qualification and raw evidence](https://sc.talos.nvidia.com/view/home/scratch.yanxu_libs/cudnn_frontend/.te-cp-20261012/results/te_frost_d128_nozero_crossnode_v164_qualified.json).

## D128 16K complete CP at the published head

Rebuilt `cf04d4e1` binaries with unchanged Roman `33327862` kernels complete **B32/S16384/Hq32/Hkv8/D128, BF16 causal compact THD, CP4/A2A, 524288 tokens** on one production B200 node. The same six-order protocol passes **288 full O/dQ/dK/dV comparisons, 18 telemetry windows and 72 fresh workers**; maximum relative RMS is 0.003663. Untimed audits confirm three versus zero output fills in every FROST arm/rank.

| FROST: initialize | FROST: omit fills | FA4 | Paired omit/initialize | Paired omit/FA4 |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 73.021 ms | 72.806 ms | 69.168 ms | -0.47% | +5.14% |

The initialization option is faster in 5/6 paired rounds and remains slower than FA4 in all six. This is one shape/node result from the published build, not a new original-grid win or evidence for other communication methods. Only the native reference uses B8 chunks; actual CP uses the complete shape. [Published-head 16K qualification](https://sc.talos.nvidia.com/view/home/scratch.yanxu_libs/cudnn_frontend/.te-cp-20261012/results/te_frost_d128_nozero_cp16k_v165_qualified.json).

The [rolling explanation and evidence](https://sc.talos.nvidia.com/view/home/scratch.yanxu_libs/cudnn_frontend/.te-cp-20261012/explainer-20261014/context-parallel-optimizations.en.html) retains earlier-head measurements and separate composition experiments with their source identities and limitations.

# Checklist

- [x] I have read and followed the contributing guidelines
- [ ] The functionality is complete
- [x] I have commented the nontrivial implementation details
- [x] I have made corresponding documentation changes
- [ ] My changes generate no new warnings
- [x] I have added focused tests
- [ ] New and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes

Draft pending human author review, stable FE export ABI and the remaining integration qualification.

## Follow-up D128 kernel synchronization qualification

[cuDNN Frontend #1698](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1698) repairs terminal dQ barrier-phase reuse in the dense and THD FROST D128 backward kernels, including the grouped-query routes. Its exact-source regression reproduces pre-fix Missing wait reports and passes 70 ordinary tests plus all eight cases under each of racecheck and synccheck after the repair. Unfiltered memcheck qualification remains pending because of a retained CUDA runtime-recompilation API warning.

The complete-CP timings above remain attributed to their stated FE/kernel snapshots, before this repair. Repaired 8K and 2K CP4/A2A remeasurements are reported separately below; the full current-FE package remains outside that qualification. [Repair validation and limitations](https://sc.talos.nvidia.com/view/home/scratch.yanxu_libs/cudnn_frontend/.te-cp-20261012/results/frost_credit_pr_v295_result.json).

## Repaired D128 8K complete CP remeasurement

A new complete CP4/A2A run uses the qualified packed terminal-credit repair, AST-equivalent to [FE #1698](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1698), on the frozen FE197 integration with #1696 and #1690. Only that packed kernel changes; TE native binaries, all other FE inputs and communication remain identical across the four providers. This is a new comparison with the repaired dependency, not a measurement of repair overhead against an unrepaired arm.

Workload: **B64/S8192/Hq32/Hkv8/D128, BF16 causal compact THD, 524288 tokens, CP4/A2A**. Four production B200 GPUs use 148 SMs, default 1000 W limits and NV18 links; cuDNN 9.27.0.42, CUDA 13.2-built TE, CuTeDSL 4.8 cu13, FA4 `4.0.0b35.dev1+gbb25ba3`. Warm eager timing includes forward, backward, helpers and communication and reports the slowest rank.

| Provider | Median complete-CP latency |
| --- | ---: |
| cuDNN backend | 48.132 ms |
| FROST backward; cuDNN forward | 45.110 ms |
| FROST forward and backward | 44.823 ms |
| FlashAttention 4 | 43.759 ms |

Paired latency changes: backward-only/FA4 **+3.03%**; combined/FA4 **+2.30%**; combined/backward-only **-0.81%**; combined/cuDNN **-6.88%**. Negative means lower latency. Percentages are medians of four paired round ratios. The combined path is faster than FA4 in **0/4** orders.

All **256 complete output/gradient comparisons**, 64 fresh workers and 48 timing windows pass, with maximum relative RMS 0.003660. Actual packed-GQA backward route, forward engine, source/binary hashes, output-fill audits and telemetry/stability gates are checked. A separately versioned collector corrects only an expected worker-status spelling; the frozen workloads, measurements and all admission gates are unchanged.

This is one coordinate on one node, not an original-grid win rate or full qualification of the current FE package. The earlier results retain their own frozen-source attribution; the repaired 2K remeasurement follows below. Public current-upstream memcheck and the remaining integration graduation requirements above remain pending. [Repaired CP qualification](https://sc.talos.nvidia.com/view/home/scratch.yanxu_libs/cudnn_frontend/.te-cp-20261012/results/te_frost_forward_cp_v299_qualified.json) · [Collector correction](https://sc.talos.nvidia.com/view/home/scratch.yanxu_libs/cudnn_frontend/.te-cp-20261012/results/te_frost_forward_cp_v299_collector_correction.json).

## Repaired D128 2K complete CP remeasurement

The same repaired FE dependency and unchanged TE binaries now complete the four-provider comparison at **B256/S2048/Hq32/Hkv8/D128, BF16 causal compact THD, 524288 tokens, CP4/A2A**. The dependency is frozen FE197 + #1696/#1690 with the qualified packed terminal-credit repair, AST-equivalent to [FE #1698](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1698). All providers use the same TE communication implementation.

Four production B200 GPUs use 148 SMs, default 1000 W and NV18 links; cuDNN 9.27.0.42, CUDA 13.2-built TE, CuTeDSL 4.8 cu13, FA4 `4.0.0b35.dev1+gbb25ba3`. Warm eager latency includes forward, backward, helpers and communication and reports the slowest rank. This coordinate runs on a different node from the repaired 8K result above.

| Provider | Median complete-CP latency |
| --- | ---: |
| cuDNN backend | 26.017 ms |
| FROST backward; cuDNN forward | 24.493 ms |
| FROST forward and backward | 24.287 ms |
| FlashAttention 4 | 25.559 ms |

Paired latency changes: backward-only/FA4 **-4.16%**; combined/FA4 **-5.01%**; combined/backward-only **-0.83%**; combined/cuDNN **-6.69%**. Negative means lower latency. These are medians of four paired round ratios; all four orders favor the combined path for every comparison.

All **256 complete output/gradient comparisons**, 64 fresh workers and 48 timing windows pass (maximum relative RMS 0.003662). Actual packed-GQA backward and forward routes, source/binary hashes, output-fill audits, hardware telemetry and timing stability are checked.

The repaired 2K and 8K results establish gains at these two bounded coordinates; 8K remains 2.30% slower than FA4. They do not establish an original-324-grid win rate, measure repair overhead against an unrepaired arm, or qualify the entire current FE package. Earlier D256 measurements retain their stated source versions. Stable FE export/packaging, public current-upstream memcheck and the remaining integration qualification remain pending. [Repaired 2K qualification and frozen evidence](https://sc.talos.nvidia.com/view/home/scratch.yanxu_libs/cudnn_frontend/.te-cp-20261012/results/te_frost_forward_cp_v304_qualified.json).

## D256 CP8 AllGather complete attention comparison

At **B64/S8192/Hq32/Hkv8/D256, BF16 causal THD, 524288 tokens, CP8/AllGather**, the integrated OSS backward reduces latency relative to the cuDNN backend, but remains slower than FA4. Forward stays on cuDNN; #3705 forward is not enabled. All providers use the same TE communication implementation.

Eight production B200 GPUs use 148 SMs each, default 1000 W limits and NV18 links. The frozen environment is TE forward-v195 (equivalent native backward from this head), FE197 + #1696/#1690 + the packed D128 terminal-credit repair (D256 kernel unchanged), cuDNN 9.27.0.42, CUDA 13.2-built TE, CuTeDSL 4.8 cu13, and FA4 `4.0.0b35.dev1+gbb25ba3`. Warm eager latency includes forward, backward, helpers and communication and reports the slowest rank.

| Provider | Median complete-CP latency | Peak allocated memory per rank |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| cuDNN backend | 77.112 ms | 54.52 GiB |
| FROST backward; cuDNN forward | 70.483 ms | 46.52 GiB |
| FlashAttention 4 | 67.895 ms | 24.52 GiB |

Median paired latency change: FROST/cuDNN **-8.86%**; FROST/FA4 **+3.79%**. Negative means lower latency. FROST is faster than cuDNN in 6/6 orders and faster than FA4 in 0/6. The prior CP4 advantage does not extend to this CP8 coordinate; the memory gap also remains.

All **576 full output/gradient comparisons** pass (maximum relative RMS 0.005357), along with **96 independent CPU FP64 comparisons** through actual small-shape CP8 (maximum relative RMS 0.005143). Six provider permutations use 18 fresh eight-rank process sets, 144 workers and 18 admitted timing windows. Source/binary/route checks, 1000 W/NV18 hardware checks, sampled HBM-clock/temperature/throttle checks, and stability gates pass. This is a one-node complete-CP screen, not a cross-node result or original-324-grid win. Earlier CP4 results keep their own frozen source and protocol attribution. [CP8 qualification and frozen evidence](https://sc.talos.nvidia.com/view/home/scratch.yanxu_libs/cudnn_frontend/.te-cp-20261012/results/te_frost_allgather_cp8_v313_qualified.json).

+def _case(dim, thd, unequal, causal, seed=31, bottom_right=False, kv_length=None, q_length=None):
+    generator = torch.Generator(device="cpu").manual_seed(seed)
+    q_lengths, k_lengths = ((129, 63), (193, 97)) if unequal else ((128, 128), (256, 256))
+    if q_length is not None:
+        assert not unequal

+    if kv_length is not None:
+        assert not unequal
+        k_lengths = (kv_length, kv_length)
+    heads, kv_heads = 4, 1
+    inputs, expected = [], []
+    for sq, sk in zip(q_lengths, k_lengths):
+
+        def draw(s, h):
+            return (torch.randn(s, h, dim, generator=generator) * 0.5).bfloat16()
+
+        q, k, v, do = draw(sq, heads), draw(sk, kv_heads), draw(sk, kv_heads), draw(sq, heads)
+        qr, kr, vr = (x.double().transpose(0, 1).requires_grad_() for x in (q, k, v))
+        scores = (qr @ kr.repeat_interleave(heads // kv_heads, 0).transpose(-1, -2)) * dim**-0.5
+        if causal:
+            scores = scores.masked_fill(
+                torch.arange(sk)[None, :]
+                > torch.arange(sq)[:, None] + (sk - sq if bottom_right else 0),
+                -torch.inf,
+            )
+        # Bottom-right Q > KV has keyless leading rows: their output/gradient is zero.
+        keyless = torch.isneginf(scores).all(dim=-1, keepdim=True)
+        probabilities = scores.masked_fill(keyless, 0).softmax(-1).masked_fill(keyless, 0)
+        result = probabilities @ vr.repeat_interleave(heads // kv_heads, 0)
+        grads = torch.autograd.grad(result, (qr, kr, vr), do.transpose(0, 1).double())
+        inputs.append((q, k, v, do))
+        expected.append(tuple(x.transpose(0, 1).detach() for x in grads))
+    combine = torch.cat if thd else torch.stack
+    q, k, v, do = (combine([row[i] for row in inputs]).cuda() for i in range(4))
+    reference = tuple(combine([row[i] for row in expected]) for i in range(3))
+    prefixes = [
+        torch.tensor([0, lengths[0], sum(lengths)], device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32)
+        for lengths in (q_lengths, k_lengths)
+    ]

+"""Prepare cuDNN OSS backward plans for TE's native dispatcher.
+
+Only preparation enters Python. The registry entry is the compiled TVM-FFI
+function for the complete backward chain, including its scratch initialization.
+The private FE prepared-plan adapter is deliberately confined to this module.
+"""
+
+from functools import partial
+from importlib.metadata import PackageNotFoundError, version
+import logging
+
+_LOG = logging.getLogger("transformer_engine.frost")
+_OWNERS = {}
+_ROLES = ("q", "k", "v", "o", "do", "stats", "dq", "dk", "dv")
+_ORIGIN_ROLES = ("q", "k", "v", "o", "do", "dq", "dk", "dv", "stats")
+_POINTER_ROLES = _ROLES + ("seq_q", "seq_kv") + tuple("ragged_" + r for r in _ORIGIN_ROLES)
+_ENGINES = {128: 20609, 256: 20607}
+
+
+def _declarations(batch, heads, kv_heads, sq, sk, dim, tq, thd, q_pitch=0, kv_pitch=0):
+    """Logical BHSD declarations over TE's BSHD or packed token-major storage."""
+    result = {}
+    for role in _ROLES:
+        kv = role in ("k", "v", "dk", "dv")
+        h, s = (kv_heads, sk) if kv else (heads, sq)
+        if role == "stats":
+            shape = (batch, heads, sq, 1)
+            stride = (tq * heads, 1, heads, 1) if thd else (heads * sq, sq, 1, 1)
+        else:
+            pitch = (kv_pitch if kv else q_pitch) or s
+            shape, stride = (batch, h, s, dim), (pitch * h * dim, dim, h * dim, 1)
+        result[role] = (shape, stride)
+    return result
+
+
+def _native_metadata(spec, dim, thd, expected_prefix):
+    """Refuse an unfamiliar prepared ABI instead of dropping optional operands."""
+    from cudnn.frost.compiled_cache import positional_entry
+    import tvm_ffi
+
+    if (
+        spec.name != f"sdpa_bwd_sm100_d{dim}"
+        or spec.scale_log2
+        or spec.packed_tile_groups
+        or bool(spec.length_form) != thd
+    ):
+        raise RuntimeError("Unsupported cuDNN OSS prepared backward contract")
+    roles = tuple(spec.roles)
+    expected = _POINTER_ROLES if thd else _ROLES + (("seq_kv", "delta") if dim == 256 else ())
+    if roles != expected or len(spec.operands) != len(roles):
+        raise RuntimeError(f"Unsupported cuDNN OSS operand order: {roles}")
+    native = positional_entry(spec.artifact.entry)
+    if not isinstance(native, tvm_ffi.Function):
+        raise RuntimeError("cuDNN OSS must expose a compiled native TVM-FFI entry")
+    if thd:
+        bound = getattr(spec.fn, "entry", None)
+        if not isinstance(bound, partial) or tuple(bound.args) != expected_prefix:
+            raise RuntimeError("Unsupported cuDNN OSS packed backward prefix")
+    elif expected_prefix:
+        raise RuntimeError("Dense backward cannot have a packed prefix")
+    metadata = [1, int(spec.workspace_bytes), int(thd), len(expected_prefix), len(roles)]
+    metadata.extend(expected_prefix)
+    for role, operand in zip(roles, spec.operands):
+        if operand is None:
+            metadata.extend((-1, 0, 1))
+            continue
+        if role not in _POINTER_ROLES or operand.opaque_bytes or operand.packed_tile_bytes:
+            raise RuntimeError(f"Unsupported cuDNN OSS operand: {role}")
+        span = int(operand.span) * int(operand.itemsize)
+        if role in ("seq_q", "seq_kv"):
+            span += 4  # TE supplies B+1 cumulative lengths, lens_form=3.
+        if span <= 0 or span > 2**63 - 1:
+            raise RuntimeError("cuDNN OSS operand byte span is not representable")
+        metadata.extend((_POINTER_ROLES.index(role), span, int(operand.alignment)))
+    return native, metadata
+
+
+def get_frost_attention_backward(
+    key,
+    batch,
+    heads,
+    kv_heads,
+    sq,
+    sk,
+    dim,
+    tq,
+    tk,
+    thd,
+    causal,
+    scale,
+    device,
+    bottom_right=False,
+    q_pitch=0,
+    kv_pitch=0,
+):
+    """Compile a graph declaration and register its native chain; allocate no data."""
+    try:
+        import cudnn
+        from cuda.bindings import runtime
+        import tvm_ffi
+    except ImportError as error:
+        _LOG.warning("cuDNN OSS attention dependency unavailable: %s", error)
+        return False
+
+    from packaging.version import Version
+
+    try:
+        dsl_version = Version(version("nvidia-cutlass-dsl"))
+    except PackageNotFoundError:
+        _LOG.warning("cuDNN OSS attention requires nvidia-cutlass-dsl >= 4.8.0")
+        return False
+    if dsl_version < Version("4.8.0"):
+        _LOG.warning("cuDNN OSS attention requires nvidia-cutlass-dsl >= 4.8.0")
+        return False
+    if dim not in _ENGINES or (thd and dim != 128):
+        return False
+    if bottom_right and (dim != 256 or not causal):
+        return False
+    if q_pitch or kv_pitch:
+        if thd or dim != 256 or q_pitch < sq or kv_pitch < sk:
+            return False
+    from cutlass.base_dsl.version_info import CUDA_VERSION
+
+    if CUDA_VERSION.major < 13:
+        _LOG.warning("cuDNN OSS backward requires the CUDA 13 flavor: nvidia-cutlass-dsl[cu13]")
+        return False
+    error, current = runtime.cudaGetDevice()
+    if int(error) != 0 or int(current) != device:
+        raise RuntimeError("cuDNN OSS preparation must use the calling CUDA device")
+    graph = cudnn.pygraph(
+        io_data_type=cudnn.data_type.BFLOAT16,
+        intermediate_data_type=cudnn.data_type.FLOAT,
+        compute_data_type=cudnn.data_type.FLOAT,
+    )
+    declarations = _declarations(batch, heads, kv_heads, sq, sk, dim, tq, thd, q_pitch, kv_pitch)
+    refs = {}
+
+    def attach(role, tensor):
+        if not thd:
+            return
+        kv = role in ("k", "v", "dk", "dv")
+        h = kv_heads if kv else heads
+        offset = graph.tensor(
+            name=role + "_origin",
+            dim=[batch + 1, 1, 1, 1],
+            stride=[1, 1, 1, 1],
+            data_type=cudnn.data_type.INT32,
+        )
+        tensor.set_ragged_offset(offset)
+        tensor.set_ragged_offset_multiplier(h if role == "stats" else h * dim)
+
+    for role in _ROLES[:6]:
+        shape, stride = declarations[role]
+        refs[role] = graph.tensor(
+            name=role,
+            dim=shape,
+            stride=stride,
+            data_type=cudnn.data_type.FLOAT if role == "stats" else cudnn.data_type.BFLOAT16,
+        )
+        attach(role, refs[role])
+    lengths = {}
+    if thd:
+        for role in ("q", "kv"):
+            lengths[role] = graph.tensor(
+                name="length_" + role,
+                dim=[batch, 1, 1, 1],
+                stride=[1, 1, 1, 1],
+                data_type=cudnn.data_type.INT32,
+            )
+    outputs = graph.sdpa_backward(
+        q=refs["q"],
+        k=refs["k"],
+        v=refs["v"],
+        o=refs["o"],
+        dO=refs["do"],
+        stats=refs["stats"],
+        attn_scale=scale,
+        use_causal_mask=causal and not bottom_right,
+        use_causal_mask_bottom_right=causal and bottom_right,
+        use_padding_mask=thd,
+        seq_len_q=lengths.get("q"),
+        seq_len_kv=lengths.get("kv"),
+        max_total_seq_len_q=tq if thd else None,
+        max_total_seq_len_kv=tk if thd else None,
+        use_deterministic_algorithm=False,
+    )
+    for role, tensor in zip(_ROLES[6:], outputs):
+        shape, stride = declarations[role]
+        tensor.set_output(True).set_data_type(cudnn.data_type.BFLOAT16)
+        tensor.set_dim(shape).set_stride(stride)
+        attach(role, tensor)
+    try:
+        graph.validate()
+        graph.build_operation_graph()
+        try:
+            graph.create_execution_plan(_ENGINES[dim], {})
+        except ValueError as error:
+            if "no python engine on this graph owns engine_id" not in str(error):
+                raise
+            _LOG.warning("Installed cuDNN Frontend lacks the requested OSS engine: %s", error)
+            return False
+        graph.build_plans()
+    except (NotImplementedError, cudnn.cudnnGraphNotSupportedError) as error:
+        _LOG.warning("cuDNN OSS attention declined this declaration: %s", error)
+        return False
+    spec = graph._compiled_plans[graph._plan_index]._prepared.spec
+    prefix = (min(batch * sq, tq), min(batch * sk, tk), tq, tk, sq, sk, 0) if thd else ()
+    native, metadata = _native_metadata(spec, dim, thd, prefix)
+    if spec.device_index != device or float(spec.scale) != float(scale):
+        raise RuntimeError("cuDNN OSS plan device/scale differs from its TE declaration")
+    # Keep the graph, compiled owner and shared library alive through graph replay.
+    _OWNERS[key] = graph
+    tvm_ffi.register_global_func(key, native, override=False)
+    return " ".join(str(value) for value in metadata)

**Codex bot review — gpt-6-astra**

Reviewed `cf04d4e11821b3b93b76915a03637bc2b572b460`. Thank you for your contribution! Comment-only review, as requested.

I did not find a new correctness blocker in the supported scope. The separation between cached declarations and per-call pointers/stream/workspace looks sound. Keeping the complete native backward chain, checking the uniform-layout promise on device on every execution, and restricting output-fill removal to a separately guarded strict-mode contract are the right boundaries.

Two follow-ups:

1. **[P2] Connect the new regression suite to a qualified QA target before graduating the draft.** `qa/L0_pytorch_unittest/test.sh` explicitly enumerates attention test files, and no checked-in QA launcher currently invokes `test_frost_attn.py`. Simply adding this file does not give the bridge or the no-zero policy ongoing CI coverage. A dedicated SM100 target with the bridge enabled and compatible FE/DSL dependencies would be sufficient; it should verify that the native-route tests actually execute, including the isolated metadata-guard children. This need not impose the experimental dependency stack on every ordinary L0 lane.

2. **[P3] Qualify the D256 bottom-right rectangular support statement and retain a decline/fallback test.** With `S_q=256, S_kv=128`, uniform THD forward works, but the equivalent dense FE backward declaration rejects `max_s_q > max_s_kv`. I verified that mode 1 correctly falls back with correct gradients (including exactly zero dQ on the leading keyless rows), while mode 2 reports the unsupported declaration. Dense BSHD is rejected by the existing forward path before this bridge. This is a support/documentation boundary, not a silent numerical failure; the current wording should make clear that rectangular support does not include both orientations.

Validation performed independently on one SM100 GPU:

- All **61 committed tests passed**, including changed bindings/streams, all tested AllGather step geometries, poisoned CUDA-graph replay, actual output-fill counts, and all five isolated invalid-metadata checks.
- **8 additional GPU checks passed** for D128 MHA/GQA with physical gaps and an empty sequence, dense MHA, and repeated replay through supported/fallback routes. Gradients were checked against CPU FP64 references.
- Separately verified the D256 Q-longer-than-KV strict decline and numerically correct THD fallback described above.
- A small alternating no-zero off/on measurement at `B=2, Hq/Hkv=4/1, D=128, S=128/1024` showed the intended host-submission reduction and no observed replay regression. Gradients were checked again after timing and poisoned replay. This is not a distributed-CP performance qualification.

I verified exact-head Python/test imports and reused the author's rebuilt native binaries after checking their hashes and matching native source snapshots; this was not an independent clean build. I did not independently rerun multi-GPU CP, JAX, the full L0 matrix, or Compute Sanitizer. The draft's stated stable-FE-export and broader-qualification work therefore remains relevant.
